summary: Unpinned remote code fetched from unpkg CDN and eval'd on CLI invocation and library import
details: The package fetches JavaScript from the unpinned URL https://unpkg.com/use-m/use.js and passes the response to eval. This happens via ensureUseM(), which is invoked from the bin entrypoints (hive, solve, task, etc.) and at the top level of src/lib.mjs (guarded only by a typeof globalThis.use check). Many other.lib.mjs modules import src/lib.mjs, so any downstream package that imports these library modules also triggers the unpinned unpkg fetch+eval at load time. Because the URL has no version pin, unpkg resolves it to whatever the current use-m npm package publishes, meaning whoever controls the use-m package (or a poisoned CDN cache entry) can inject arbitrary JavaScript that executes with the installer's user privileges on every CLI run and on every import of the affected library modules. The fallback URL is version-pinned but is only reached if the primary fetch fails.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
